note: Oral S1P1 agonists (ozanimod, etrasimod; mocravimod's UC trial was terminated) taken into moderate-to-severe UC on mouse colitis models and blood lymphocyte counts.
label: Ulcerative colitis (S1P1)

engagement.note: FTY720 sequestered circulating lymphocytes in colitic IL-10-/- mice; no patient comparison yet.
engagement.short: FTY720 sequesters lymphocytes in colitic mice
engagement.quote: Single-dose administration of FTY720 resulted in the sequestration of circulating lymphocytes within the secondary lymphoid tissues.
engagement.judgement: Opening entry: fingolimod is not a member, so product_in_model false; it dates the blood-lymphocyte readout in a colitis model.

engagement.magnitude_basis: % fall in circulating lymphocytes (mouse 0.6 mg/kg 51%; patients 1 mg 49%)
engagement.confidence_note: Rodent figure from Scott 2016 full text (PMC4867749) via a quote extraction; the 51% is 24 h after the last 0.6 mg/kg dose in a disease-model study, not a matched dose.
engagement.note: Ozanimod cut circulating lymphocytes 51% in mice; UC patients' counts fell 49% at 1 mg in TOUCHSTONE.
engagement.quote: At week 8, absolute lymphocyte counts declined 49% from baseline in the group that received 1 mg of ozanimod and 32% from baseline in the group that received 0.5 mg.
engagement.reason: Lymphocytes fell in patients as in mice
engagement.judgement: Paired: Scott 2016 (epub 2016-04-28): '0.6 mg·kg−1 RPC1063 reduced the number of lymphocytes by 51%'. Neither paper states the comparison. Lymphocyte count scored downstream (physiology after S1P1 internalisation, not occupancy). Healthy volunteers agree (Tran 2017: median 65-68% fall at 1-1.5 mg); etrasimod UC patients ~50% (FDA review 216956).

dose.model: Rodent PK: half-life supporting once-daily dosing (ozanimod)
dose.note: Rodent PK predicted a half-life fit for once-daily dosing; no human data yet.
dose.quote: RPC1063 showed high oral bioavailability and volume of distribution, and a circulatory half-life that supports once daily dosing.
dose.judgement: Regimen prediction counted as a dose target (the brief lists 'regimen'). No rodent exposure or EC50 projected to a human dose in the abstract.

dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level; rodent half-life value not extracted, so direction only.
dose.model: Rodent PK: half-life supporting once-daily dosing (ozanimod)
dose.note: Human half-life 17-21 h held up once-daily dosing; 1 mg once daily induced remission in TOUCHSTONE.
dose.short: Human half-life 17-21 h; once daily worked
dose.quote: Ozanimod exhibited linear PK, high steady-state volume of distribution (73-101 L/kg), moderate oral clearance (204-227 L/h), and an elimination half-life of approximately 17 to 21 hours.
dose.judgement: Reached and worked (1 mg QD, TOUCHSTONE 2016) so same; the human PK is dated to the FIH paper (epub 2017-08-07). FIH trial registration not found in the abstract; registry_date null.

dose.magnitude_basis: AUC multiple of MRHD at NOAEL
dose.confidence_note: Patient side is the same review's clinical safety sections (bradycardia, AV block, liver tests are the class harms), read by grep only.
dose.note: Rats and dogs tolerated 738- and 446-fold the human 2 mg exposure; UC patients dosed at 2 mg without liver or thymus harm.
dose.quote: No adverse effects were observed in rats or dogs at exposures up to 738- and 446-fold, respectively, the exposure at the maximum recommended human dose (MRHD) of 2 mg/day (based on AUC comparison).
dose.reason: Stated tolerability margin held in patients
dose.judgement: Decision 16 entry: a stated margin that held is same, margin_stated true; a different system from rodent PK, so model_change. The same review says the mouse transfer-colitis effect 'generally occurred at ≥ 3 mg/kg/day (approximately 2.4-fold the clinical dose of 2 mg/day, based on HED)': patients responded below the model's HED target, an over-prediction of about 2.4x not scored because the review does not call it one and HED scaling is crude. Model rat/dog tox start year unknown; 2016 used as a proxy.

efficacy.note: FTY720 healed established colitis in IL-10-/- mice; mocravimod (KRP-203) did the same in 2007.
efficacy.short: FTY720 heals colitis in IL-10-/- mice
efficacy.quote: Treatment of established colitis in IL-10-/- mice with FTY720 ameliorated the colitis, probably as a result of decreasing the number of lymphocytes in the colonic mucosa and an associated reduction in IFN-gamma production.
efficacy.judgement: Song 2008 (doi 10.1124/jpet.106.119172, epub 2007-09-26): 'KRP-203 significantly inhibits ongoing IL-10(-/-) colitis'. Mocravimod's UC phase 2 NCT01375179 terminated at 27 patients with no results and no reason posted, so the IL-10-/- model was never compared for a member drug.

efficacy.model: TNBS and CD4+CD45RBhi transfer colitis mice (ozanimod)
efficacy.note: Ozanimod cleared TNBS and transfer colitis in mice; TOUCHSTONE gave 16% vs 6% remission at 1 mg, confirmed by TRUE NORTH and ELEVATE.
efficacy.quote: In this preliminary trial, ozanimod at a daily dose of 1 mg resulted in a slightly higher rate of clinical remission of ulcerative colitis than placebo.
efficacy.reason: Mouse colitis cleared; patients reached remission
efficacy.judgement: Paired, not stated: Scott 2016 abstract 'Oral RPC1063 reduced inflammation and disease parameters in all three autoimmune disease models'. Not neg: no member failed. Etrasimod's CD4+CD45RBhi data were filed (FDA review 216956) and ELEVATE matched them. Mocravimod's terminated trial has no result to score. Amiselimod (not a member) is ignored.

safety.note: Mouse genetics tied bradycardia to S1P3, predicting S1P1-selective agonists would spare heart rate.
safety.quote: The sustained bradycardia induced by S1P receptor non-selective immunosuppressive agonists in wild-type mice is abolished in S1P(3)-/- mice, whereas S1P(1)-selective agonist does not produce bradycardia.
safety.judgement: The class's S1P3-sparing design rested on this; Scott 2016 claims selectivity 'could result in improved safety outcomes in the clinic'.

safety.note: S1P3-sparing ozanimod still slowed human hearts after the first dose; etrasimod later did too, by up to 19 bpm.
safety.short: S1P3-sparing ozanimod still slows the heart
safety.quote: A dose-dependent negative chronotropic effect was observed following the first dose, with the dose-escalation regimen attenuating the first-dose negative chronotropic effect.
safety.judgement: v3 drops the v2 2012 entry: siponimod (Gergely 2012) is not a member. First member datum is ozanimod FIH (epub 2017-08-07). The FDA ozanimod review (2020) later states it: 'Early literature suggests that these effects were modulated by S1P3, but later literature ... suggests involvement of other S1P subtypes, including S1P1.' Etrasimod dog telemetry was also silent (NOEL 350 mg/kg) while healthy subjects fell up to 19.4 bpm.

safety.magnitude_basis: IKACh EC50 vs clinical Cmax (EC50 6x below steady-state Cmax)
safety.confidence_note: Study APD334.TS.011 date not given in the review; retrodiction inferred from its use of ozanimod and fingolimod, whose bradycardia was known, as comparators.
safety.model: Human atrial cardiomyocyte IKACh (GIRK) patch clamp
safety.note: Etrasimod, ozanimod and fingolimod opened atrial IKACh at clinical concentrations; FDA tied this to the first-dose heart rate fall.
safety.short: Human atrial cells reproduce heart-rate effect
safety.quote: In an in vitro assay using human atrial cardiomyocytes, etrasimod activated IKAch channels at concentrations less than the predicted steady state Cmax and Ctrough values at the clinical etrasimod dose of 2 mg/day
safety.reason: Human atrial cells reproduce known bradycardia
safety.judgement: Scored retro, not same: run after first-dose bradycardia was known for the class. Review: HR fell -3.3 to -19.4 bpm in healthy subjects and -7.3 to -9.4 bpm in UC patients after the first 2 mg dose. Not the amiselimod GIRK work (not a member).

safety.confidence_note: Study date not given in the review; 2012 is a proxy for IND-enabling work before ozanimod's first-in-human study (Tran 2017).
safety.note: IND-enabling monkey CV study: ozanimod cut heart rate 20% and diastolic pressure 20% at the top dose.
safety.quote: Heart rate decreased by 20% and the R-R interval increased by 37% at the highest dose given and persisted for 24 hours after dosing.
safety.judgement: Opener at a proxy first-use year; the study is only public through the 2020 review.

safety.magnitude_basis: first-dose heart rate fall; diastolic BP fell in monkeys but rose in patients
safety.confidence_note: Comparison made in the MS NDA (patients with relapsing MS); grep of the summary review only, the pharm/tox review is not in the bundle.
safety.note: FDA set the monkey heart-rate fall beside patients' bradycardia; the monkeys' diastolic pressure fall was opposite to patients' rise.
safety.short: Monkey heart-rate fall seen in patients
safety.quote: Reduction in heart rate and increased blood pressure are seen in patients treated with ozanimod.
safety.reason: Heart rate matched; blood pressure opposite
safety.judgement: Scored same with source_calls_it partial: heart rate matched in direction (the class's main first-dose harm), blood pressure went the other way. Unlike the S1P3-KO mouse, the filed system predicted ozanimod's bradycardia. Imported from MS.

safety.confidence_note: Study date not given; 2014 is a proxy for IND-enabling safety pharmacology before etrasimod's first-in-human studies.
safety.note: Single oral etrasimod doses up to 350 mg/kg had no cardiovascular effect in dogs.
safety.quote: A single oral dose of etrasimod did not produce acute CNS or clinically relevant respiratory effects in rats (NOELs: 350 mg/kg/day) or cardiovascular effects in dogs (NOEL: 350 mg/kg/day).
safety.judgement: Opener at a proxy year; public only through the 2023 review.

safety.magnitude_basis: first-dose heart rate change (dogs none at NOEL 350 mg/kg; UC patients -7.2 bpm)
safety.confidence_note: Whether beagles show S1P1-mediated first-dose bradycardia was not verified; the review places the dog result and the clinical heart-rate fall in one paragraph but does not call the dog study a miss.
safety.note: Dogs showed no cardiovascular effect, yet UC patients' heart rate fell 7.2 bpm after the first 2 mg dose.
safety.short: Dogs silent; patients' heart rate fell
safety.quote: After the first dose of VELSIPITY 2 mg, subjects with UC experienced the greatest mean decrease from baseline in heart rate of 7.2 bpm at Hour 3 in UC-1 and Hour 2 in UC-2.
safety.judgement: Contra: silence on a harm a dog's heart can show (dogs have atrial GIRK channels), at a NOEL far above clinical exposure. Paired within the review, so comparison_stated false. The review credits the human atrial myocyte assay (already in the draft) for the mechanism.

safety.confidence_note: Study date not given; 2014 proxy. Heterologous cell line, coded ex_vivo as the nearest model_kind.
safety.note: Etrasimod had no significant effect on hERG current (59% inhibition at 3 µM, IC50 an estimated 4-12x Cmax).
safety.quote: In a standard battery of nonclinical safety pharmacology studies, etrasimod had no significant effects on hERG channel current in vitro, cardiovascular function in dogs, CNS parameters in rats, or respiratory function in rats.

safety.magnitude_basis: hERG call vs thorough QT result at 4 mg (2x clinical dose)
safety.confidence_note: The review's own estimate puts the hERG IC50 at 4-12x Cmax, below the usual 30x margin, so the assay's 'no significant effect' call is softer than it reads. TQT date and registration not looked up.
safety.note: The thorough QT study found no significant QTc prolongation at a supratherapeutic 4 mg, as the hERG assay predicted.
safety.short: No QTc prolongation, as hERG predicted
safety.quote: In the thorough QT study, etrasimod was not associated with significant QTc prolonging effect at a supratherapeutic dose of 4 mg QD on Day 14
safety.reason: hERG call held in the TQT study
safety.judgement: Off-target safety, single modality so no modality field. Paired within the review (comparison_stated false). Ozanimod's TQT (metabolite CC112273) was also negative but no ozanimod hERG datum was in the bundle.

safety.confidence_note: Study dates not given; 2012 is a proxy for the IND-enabling toxicology package.
safety.note: Rat and monkey toxicology named the lung a prominent ozanimod target: macrophage infiltration, heavier lungs, faster breathing in rats.
safety.short: Rat and monkey: lung is a target
safety.quote: The lung was a prominent target of ozanimod in rat and monkey.
safety.judgement: Opener at a proxy year; public only through the 2020 review.
safety.model: Rat and monkey repeat-dose toxicology, lung (ozanimod)

safety.magnitude_basis: lung findings in animals vs FEV1 decline in patients
safety.confidence_note: Paired, not stated: FDA based its respiratory concern on prior S1P drugs in humans, not on the animal findings; animal histology (macrophage infiltration) and human spirometry are different readouts.
safety.note: Patients on ozanimod lost FEV1 dose-dependently (60 mL vs interferon at 12 months), as the animal lung findings flagged.
safety.short: Patients' FEV1 fell, as animals flagged
safety.quote: Dose-dependent reductions in absolute forced expiratory volume over 1 second (FEV1) were observed in patients treated with ZEPOSIA as early as 3 months after treatment initiation.
safety.reason: Animal lung target; patient FEV1 fell
safety.judgement: Paired within the same NDA (MS); direction only. Etrasimod's rat lung histiocytosis and its UC-1 FEV1 decline are the same pattern but belong to the draft's rat-dog-tox-etrasimod system, so not added here.
safety.model: Rat and monkey repeat-dose toxicology, lung (ozanimod)
